title: Finite Galois splitting into normal geometrically integral clopen components
statement: Let $e$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $B$ be a nonempty integral finite-type $e$-scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose that every local ring of $B$ is an integrally closed domain and that $B$ is geometrically reduced [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. For every field extension $F/e$ [def-pc-field-extension], the scheme $B_F=B\times_e\operatorname{Spec}F$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is Noetherian, meaning that it admits a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. There exists a finite Galois extension $e_0/e$ (finite-dimensional, separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and normal: every irreducible polynomial over $e$ with a root in $e_0$ splits over $e_0$) [def-pc-field-tower] such that the irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $Y=B_{e_0}$ form a finite nonempty disjoint covering by nonempty open and closed subschemes $X_i$. Each $X_i$, with its induced open subscheme structure, is normal (all its local rings are integrally closed domains) and geometrically integral over $e_0$, meaning that $(X_i)_E$ is integral for every field extension $E/e_0$. The projection $p:Y\to B$ is finite, etale and surjective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] [def-weil-etale-morphism] [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. If $B$ is proper over $e$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], every $X_i$ is proper over $e_0$.

proof.text: For any field extension $F/e$, finite-type base change makes $B_F$ finite type over $F$. By the definition of finite type it has a finite affine cover $\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ with each $A_a$ a finitely generated $F$-algebra. The affine Noetherian lemma makes every $A_a$ Noetherian. This proves the asserted Noetherianity for every $F$, in particular for each extension chosen below. It uses neither separatedness of $B$ nor finite degree of $F/e$.

Apply the existing component-splitting theorem to $B/e$. It gives a field extension $L/e$ whose spectrum map is finite etale and for which every irreducible component of $B_L$ has irreducible nonempty inverse image after every extension of $L$. The extension $L/e$ is finite separable: apply the etale residue-field lemma to $e\to L$ and the zero prime of $L$; the two residue fields are $e$ and $L$ themselves. Thus this $L$ satisfies the hypotheses of the finite-Galois receiving-extension theorem.

The map $p_L:B_L\to B$ is finite and etale by base change of the spectrum map in step 2. That spectrum map is surjective since both field spectra have one point; surjective base change shows that $p_L$ is surjective, so $B_L$ is nonempty. Step 1 makes $B_L$ Noetherian, and $B$ is normal integral by hypothesis. Apply the etale normal-component theorem: write $B_L$ as a finite disjoint union of nonempty clopen normal integral open subschemes $D_i$. These are exactly its irreducible components. Indeed an irreducible subset cannot meet two disjoint clopen pieces, and each $D_i$ is itself irreducible and closed; maximality therefore identifies the components with the pieces. The index set is nonempty because their union is nonempty.

proof.text: Each $D_i$ is geometrically integral over $L$. For any field $E/L$, its base change $(D_i)_E$ is the open subscheme of $B_E$ on the inverse image of $D_i$: the restriction with the restricted structure sheaf satisfies the same fibre-product universal property. Its underlying space is irreducible and nonempty by step 2 and the component identification in step 3. Since $E$ is also an extension of $e$, the hypothesis of geometric reducedness makes $B_E$ reduced. The local rings of its open subscheme $(D_i)_E$ are the same local rings, hence reduced. Thus $(D_i)_E$ is nonempty, reduced and irreducible, hence integral. This argument works for every $E/L$, not just separable or algebraic extensions.

Apply the finite-Galois receiving-extension theorem to the single finite separable extension $L/e$. Obtain a finite separable normal extension $e_0/e$ and an $e$-embedding $L\to e_0$; use this embedding for all subsequent base changes. Put $Y=B_{e_0}$ and $X_i=(D_i)_{e_0}$. Fibre-product associativity identifies $Y$ with $(B_L)_{e_0}$: both represent a map to $B$ and a compatible map to $\operatorname{Spec}e_0$. Write $q:Y\to B_L$ for the projection. Open-immersion base change and the restriction universal property identify $X_i$ with $q^{-1}(D_i)$ and its complementary open with $q^{-1}(B_L\setminus D_i)$. These inverse images are complementary because inverse image commutes with set difference and unions. Likewise their pairwise intersections are empty and their union is $Y$. Thus the $X_i$ form a finite disjoint clopen cover. For every field $E/e_0$, the same universal property gives $(X_i)_E\cong(D_i)_E$, with $E$ viewed as an $L$-field. Step 4 makes this integral. Thus every $X_i$ is geometrically integral and nonempty (take $E=e_0$). As in step 3, these integral clopen pieces are precisely the irreducible components of $Y$.

proof.text: Finite dimensionality makes the ring map $e\to e_0$ finite, so its spectrum map is finite by the affine finite-map lemma. It is etale by finite separability, and surjective because both spectra are singletons. Base change along $B\to\operatorname{Spec}e$ now proves that $p:Y\to B$ is finite, etale and surjective. To check normality as well, apply the etale normal-component theorem to this $p$: $Y$ is Noetherian by step 1 and $B$ is normal integral. It expresses $Y$ as a disjoint union of normal integral open subschemes, so every local ring of $Y$ is an integrally closed domain. Each $X_i$ is an open subscheme of $Y$, and therefore has the same local rings at its points. This proves the required normality of the $X_i$ without asserting normality after an arbitrary inseparable field extension.

Finally suppose $B/e$ is proper. Proper base change makes $Y/e_0$ proper. The open inclusion $X_i\hookrightarrow Y$ is an immersion: factor it as the identity closed immersion of $X_i$ followed by that open inclusion. Its image is closed by step 5, so the closed-image immersion criterion makes it a closed immersion. The closed-subscheme clause of the properness lemma now makes $X_i/e_0$ proper. The properness hypothesis was used only in this final step.
